full_judgment: 9. From the judgment of the trial Court, it appears that it discussed the evidence, both oral and documentary in detail and came to the clear finding that though the plaintiff claimed his possession in the suit land, he did not say either in the plaint or in his examination-in-chief as to how he possessed the suit land. The trial Court further found that PW1, i.e. the plaintiff in his cross-examination sated that he had got his pond, homestead and cultivable land in the suit land, but in the plaint, it was not stated which plot was nal plot and in which plot, there was homestead. PW I stated that the defendants had their homestead in the suit plot and they had been living there for a few years. The trial Court also noticed that PWs 3 and 4 in their examination-in-chief clearly stated that the defendants had got their ancestral homestead in the suit land. The trial Court further noticed that DWI, Abdul Latif, clearly asserted in his exanimation-in-chief that he had his homestead in the suit land and the other witnesses corroborated the fact of possession of the defendant in the suit land. The trial Court concluded that from the evidence adduced by the parties, both oral and documentary, it was defendants that both the plaintiff and the defendants were the descendants of Kerali Sardar and there was complication as to the quantum of land owned by him and who inherited what quantum of land and how the lands were transferred to his heirs and whether the plaintiff got title in the suit land and then to what extend, would depend upon the decision on the said questions. The trial Court also gave clear finding that the plaintiff failed to prove his exclusive possession in the suit land. On the above findings, the trial Court concluded   that the plaintiff either ought to have filed a suit for title with the prayer for recovery of khas possession or a suit for partition and accordingly, dismissed the suit.
